correctness.rationale: The centralizer in sl2 of every nonzero element is its line; the projectivized nilpotent locus is a split conic and the other locus its complement; each Sym^m kernel has dimension one for nilpotent x and one exactly for even m for nonnilpotent x in the declared characteristic range. The radical equations give a constant-rank vector bundle with dimension d+(s-1)r over each projective rank stratum. Thus the motivic formula follows by scissors and affine-bundle identities. Both collision algebras are perfect and centerless; nonisomorphism follows from their different irreducible highest-weight multisets after passage to an algebraic closure. Direct finite-field bracket-matrix rank computations independently support the count.

value.rationale: All-arity commuting varieties are standard, naturally defined Lie algebra moduli objects. A complete motivic profile for infinitely many nonreductive Lie algebras is more informative than a single numerical count, while the two ten-dimensional nonisomorphic examples show that even perfect, centerless algebras with a simple nonabelian Levi quotient cannot be reconstructed from all finite-field commuting-tuple zeta profiles. This distinguishes an actual structural reconstruction limit not implied by generic centralizer dimensions alone.
